review.source: Actual written N1904 and the publisher rows, reviewed against the displayed BSB by Claude (Anthropic); independent peer review recorded in the registry.

4:1.sourceText: Καὶ πάλιν ἤρξατο διδάσκειν παρὰ τὴν θάλασσαν. καὶ συνάγεται πρὸς αὐτὸν ὄχλος πλεῖστος, ὥστε αὐτὸν εἰς πλοῖον ἐμβάντα καθῆσθαι ἐν τῇ θαλάσσῃ, καὶ πᾶς ὁ ὄχλος πρὸς τὴν θάλασσαν ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς ἦσαν.
4:1.targetText: Once again Jesus began to teach beside the sea, and such a large crowd gathered around Him that He got into a boat and sat in it, while all the people crowded along the shore.

groups.note: The participle ἐμβάντα with εἰς ("embarking into") is rendered got into.
ἦσαν ("were") is rendered with the more vivid crowded.

unmappedSource.reason: The opening καί is not separately expressed in this English wording.
ἐν τῇ θαλάσσῃ ("on the sea") is not rendered; BSB says instead that He sat in the boat.
πρὸς τὴν θάλασσαν ("facing the sea") is implied in BSB's shore and not rendered separately.

unmappedTarget.reason: English names the subject; the Greek has only the verb ending of ἤρξατο.
English coordinator; ἐμβάντα (got into) is a participle, with no conjunction before καθῆσθαι.
English supplies where He sat (the boat); the Greek ἐν goes with the sea, not the boat.

4:2.sourceText: καὶ ἐδίδασκεν αὐτοὺς ἐν παραβολαῖς πολλά, καὶ ἔλεγεν αὐτοῖς ἐν τῇ διδαχῇ αὐτοῦ

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the addressees αὐτοῖς ("to them") unexpressed.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

4:3.sourceText: Ἀκούετε. ἰδοὺ ἐξῆλθεν ὁ σπείρων σπεῖραι.

groups.note: ὁ σπείρων ("the one sowing") is rendered A farmer.

unmappedSource.reason: The attention marker ἰδού ("look") is not separately expressed; Listen renders Ἀκούετε.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the possessive and the object of sowing; σπεῖραι has no written object.

4:4.sourceText: καὶ ἐγένετο ἐν τῷ σπείρειν ὃ μὲν ἔπεσεν παρὰ τὴν ὁδόν, καὶ ἦλθεν τὰ πετεινὰ καὶ κατέφαγεν αὐτό.
4:4.targetText: And as he was sowing, some seed fell along the path, and the birds came and devoured it.

unmappedSource.reason: The narrative frame ἐγένετο ("it came about") is not separately expressed.
The article of the infinitive (ἐν τῷ σπείρειν) has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
The first member of the partition is expressed without a separate μέν word.

4:5.targetText: Some fell on rocky ground, where it did not have much soil. It sprang up quickly because the soil was shallow.

4:6.targetText: But when the sun rose, the seedlings were scorched, and they withered because they had no root.

unmappedSource.reason: The article of the infinitive (διὰ τὸ μὴ ἔχειν) has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English names the understood subject; ἐκαυματίσθη has only a verb ending, and no seedling noun is written.

4:7.sourceText: καὶ ἄλλο ἔπεσεν εἰς τὰς ἀκάνθας, καὶ ἀνέβησαν αἱ ἄκανθαι καὶ συνέπνιξαν αὐτό, καὶ καρπὸν οὐκ ἔδωκεν.

The pronoun αὐτό ("it", the seed) is rendered by its referent.

4:8.targetText: Still other seed fell on good soil, where it sprouted, grew up, and produced a crop—one bearing thirtyfold, another sixtyfold, and another a hundredfold.”

groups.note: The displayed ἐν is the preposition in, G1722, not the publisher’s numeral ἓν, G1520. Together with sixty it expresses the yield rate sixtyfold.

The English growth/yield list uses comma coordination without a separately written and at these two positions.

groups.note: κατὰ μόνας is an idiom for alone.
σὺν τοῖς δώδεκα ("with the Twelve") is kept as a phrase, though BSB attaches it to alone.

English joins the two groups; the Greek links them with σύν ("with").

4:11.sourceText: καὶ ἔλεγεν αὐτοῖς Ὑμῖν τὸ μυστήριον δέδοται τῆς βασιλείας τοῦ Θεοῦ· ἐκείνοις δὲ τοῖς ἔξω ἐν παραβολαῖς τὰ πάντα γίνεται,
4:11.targetText: He replied, “The mystery of the kingdom of God has been given to you, but to those on the outside everything is expressed in parables,

groups.note: τοῖς ἔξω ("the ones outside") is rendered those on the outside.
τὰ πάντα ("all things") is rendered everything.

unmappedSource.reason: The opening καί is not separately expressed in this English wording.
BSB leaves the addressees αὐτοῖς ("to them") unexpressed.

4:12.sourceText: ἵνα βλέποντες βλέπωσιν καὶ μὴ ἴδωσιν, καὶ ἀκούοντες ἀκούωσιν καὶ μὴ συνιῶσιν, μή ποτε ἐπιστρέψωσιν καὶ ἀφεθῇ αὐτοῖς.
4:12.targetText: so that,  ‘they may be ever seeing but never perceiving, and ever hearing but never understanding; otherwise they might turn and be forgiven.’”

groups.note: βλέποντες βλέπωσιν ("seeing they may see") is an emphatic repetition, rendered may be ever seeing.
ἀκούοντες ἀκούωσιν ("hearing they may hear") is rendered ever hearing.
μή ποτε ("lest") is rendered otherwise.
ἀφεθῇ αὐτοῖς ("it be forgiven them") is rendered as the personal passive be forgiven.

4:13.sourceText: καὶ λέγει αὐτοῖς Οὐκ οἴδατε τὴν παραβολὴν ταύτην, καὶ πῶς πάσας τὰς παραβολὰς γνώσεσθε;

unmappedTarget.reason: English names the speaker; the Greek has only the verb ending of λέγει.

4:15.sourceText: οὗτοι δέ εἰσιν οἱ παρὰ τὴν ὁδὸν ὅπου σπείρεται ὁ λόγος, καὶ ὅταν ἀκούσωσιν εὐθὺς ἔρχεται ὁ Σατανᾶς καὶ αἴρει τὸν λόγον τὸν ἐσπαρμένον εἰς αὐτούς.

groups.note: As in 4:20, the copula of the metaphor is rendered as the simile are like.
The article οἱ ("those") is rendered by its referent, the seeds.
ὅταν ("when") and εὐθύς ("immediately") together are rendered As soon as.
τὸν ἐσπαρμένον ("the one sown") is rendered as a relative clause.

4:17.targetText: But they themselves have no root, and they remain for only a season. When trouble or persecution comes because of the word, they quickly fall away.

groups.note: ἐν ἑαυτοῖς ("in themselves") is rendered by BSB's themselves.

4:19.sourceText: καὶ αἱ μέριμναι τοῦ αἰῶνος καὶ ἡ ἀπάτη τοῦ πλούτου καὶ αἱ περὶ τὰ λοιπὰ ἐπιθυμίαι εἰσπορευόμεναι συνπνίγουσιν τὸν λόγον, καὶ ἄκαρπος γίνεται.

4:20.sourceText: καὶ ἐκεῖνοί εἰσιν οἱ ἐπὶ τὴν γῆν τὴν καλὴν σπαρέντες, οἵτινες ἀκούουσιν τὸν λόγον καὶ παραδέχονται καὶ καρποφοροῦσιν ἐν τριάκοντα καὶ ἐν ἑξήκοντα καὶ ἐν ἑκατόν.
